title: Harmonize accent temperature and proportional radius deltas for dense form surfaces
creator: Ariel Kim
description:
Problem: Our current token delta set for accents (primary/secondary/accent-muted) and corner radii creates visual noise in high-density forms and data tables. Multiple product teams reported inconsistent button radii and interaction contrast in compact mode which increases perceived clutter and occasionally fails low-contrast automated checks.

Goal: Produce a small, backward-compatible token surface spec that: 1) defines a single "temperature" ramp for accent colors (warm -> neutral -> cool) with accessible deltas for interactive states; 2) standardizes a proportional radius scale for dense controls (micro, compact, default) that maps to component anatomy (buttons, inputs, chips, table cells) to reduce cognitive load and implementation variance.

This ticket covers token definitions, visual examples, accessibility checks, migration notes for components, and a rollout plan for a staged console/hosted UI release.
acceptance_criteria: A token palette document exists with 5 step accent-temperature ramp and specified hex values for default, hover, pressed, and disabled states
A proportional radius scale (3 values) is defined with examples for button/input/table-cell/chip and mapping rules for density variants
Contrast checks (WCAG AA for normal text, 3:1 for UI components) pass for default and hover states; failures are flagged with recommended color adjustments
Design Sketch/FIGMA file with component overlays and migration annotations is linked
Engineering implementation notes and CSS token names are published and a PR template for component updates is created
A migration plan with canary rollout (console first, then host) and a feature-flag path for quick rollback is documented
design_notes: Introduce 'accent-temperature' token family: accent.warm.[0-4], accent.neutral.[0-4], accent.cool.[0-4]. Use neutral.2 as default accent baseline for product calls-to-action.

Interactive state rules: hover = tone step +1 with 12% overlay for emphasis; pressed = tone step +2 or 16% overlay depending on contrast target; disabled = neutral.1 with 60% opacity token for icons/text.
Radius scale: micro (4px) -> compact (8px) -> standard (12px). Map micro -> compact-mode inputs/tables, compact -> compact buttons/chips, standard -> default buttons and cards.
Introduce 'density mapping' rules in docs: when density = 'compact' components should subtract one radius step and swap to accent.neutral ramp for secondary actions.
Provide a visual diff page showing before/after high-density table, form, and button variants for product review.
engineering_notes: CSS export: provide tokens as CSS custom properties and as a JSON tokens file for runtime theming in Redwood Console
Component changes should default to new tokens behind a feature flag (design.tokens.v2026-03) so we can stage rollouts and quickly revert if regressions occur
Performance note: no runtime heavy computations; tokens are static values. Ensure server-side rendering picks up CSS variables for initial paint consistency.
Provide migration script checklist for front-end teams: 1) swap token names in style tokens map, 2) run visual diff test, 3) open PR with snapshot changes and mark for UX review
migration_plan: Phase 1 (console canary): apply tokens to Redwood Console only, expose feature flag for design QA and product teams
Phase 2 (hosted UI): enable tokens for all hosted admin surfaces after signoff and fix any visual regressions found in canary
Phase 3 (client SDK): publish tokens JSON and update SDK docs; notify platform teams with a 2-week deprecation window for legacy token names
Rollback: feature flag should toggle all token mappings; prepare hotfix branch template for urgent reversion
